ESPR READINESS CHECKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Can you still destroy unsold stock in the EU, what must you publish, and is your product passport-ready?

Pick your product, role and size. You get whether the ban on destroying unsold apparel and footwear binds you, a draft of the annual unsold-goods disclosure table built from your own numbers, and the Digital Product Passport data to start collecting now.

A first read of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR). It is not legal advice.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Destruction ban: large enterprises may not destroy unsold apparel, clothing accessories or footwear from 19 July 2026; medium-sized enterprises from 19 July 2030; micro and small enterprises are exempt.
    • 
      
  • Disclosure: enterprises that are not SMEs publish each year the number and weight of discarded unsold consumer products, the reasons, and the share per treatment route.
    • 
      
  • Passport: the Digital Product Passport is set product group by product group. Textiles are in the first wave of the Commission's working plan; the checklist is a starting list, not the final data set.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: the delegated act's exceptions to the ban, how your group counts for size, which of your items fall in a product group, final passport data fields and dates, and national enforcement rules.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
Can a fashion brand still destroy unsold clothes in the EU?

    
Not if it is a large enterprise. Under the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, large enterprises may not destroy unsold apparel, clothing accessories or footwear from 19 July 2026. Medium-sized enterprises follow from 19 July 2030, and micro and small enterprises are exempt. Destroying means disposal or energy recovery; resale, donation, remanufacture and recycling stay open.

    
What do large companies have to publish about unsold goods?

    
Enterprises that are not SMEs must publish each year the number and weight of unsold consumer products they discard, the reasons, and the share sent to preparation for reuse, remanufacture, recycling, energy recovery and disposal. This page drafts that table from your own numbers.

    
What is a Digital Product Passport?

    
A structured record of a product's materials, origin, repair and end-of-life information, reached through a QR code or similar data carrier on the product. The ESPR creates it; product-specific delegated acts decide the data and the dates. Textiles are in the first wave of the Commission's working plan.

    
Does this apply to me if I sell from outside the EU?

    
The rules attach to products placed on the EU market, so a non-EU brand selling to EU consumers is covered, usually through an importer or authorised representative in the EU. Marketplaces have their own duties.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent. Stock figures stay on your device; closing the tab discards them.

Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (analysis_run, example_loaded, summary_downloaded, csv_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device, never with any of your data, and are switched off by Do Not Track.
